svg.title: One Cohort, Five Measurable Conversion Steps
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-qualified-seller-to-serviced-wrap-funnel; chart type: funnel; title: One Cohort, Five Measurable Conversion Steps; subtitle: A 500-record sourcing cohort narrows to six funded and boarded wraps.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative six-month cohort, not observed conversion data. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Counts do not derive the $475,000 annual Base-Case revenue: annual retained interest also depends on the seasoned performing portfolio.; caption: Track losses by reason: seller mismatch, title defects, acceleration liquidity, buyer repayment capacity, and closing attrition. Do not count an application as a funded wrap.; stages: label: Screened seller records; value: 500 unique records establish the cohort denominator; numeric value: 500.0; detail: Deduplicate property and owner records, verify the trigger date, and document contact eligibility. This starting population represents 100% of the defined cohort.; label: Documented seller conversations; value: 150 conversations equal 30% of screened records; numeric value: 150.0; detail: Count only sellers who discuss debt terms and transaction objectives. The remaining 350 records never advance into documented underwriting during this cohort window.; label: Debt-and-title qualified opportunities; value: 45 opportunities equal 30% of seller conversations; numeric value: 45.0; detail: Require usable debt evidence, preliminary title findings, a priceable arrears position, and a credible acceleration response. These opportunities equal 9% of starting records.; label: Matched and underwritten wrap files; value: 12 files equal 26.7% of qualified opportunities; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Each file has a specific qualified buyer, licensed RMLO review, documented repayment analysis, and counsel-reviewed structure. These files equal 2.4% of starting records.; label: Funded and servicer-boarded wraps; value: Six closings equal 50% of underwritten files; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Count only executed closings with confirmed funding, recording submission, servicing setup, and an underlying payment schedule. Final conversion equals 1.2% of records.

text.title: One Cohort, Five Measurable Conversion Steps
text.tspan: One Cohort, Five Measurable Conversion Steps

circle.title: label: Screened seller records; value: 500 unique records establish the cohort denominator; numeric value: 500.0; detail: Deduplicate property and owner records, verify the trigger date, and document contact eligibility. This starting population represents 100% of the defined cohort.

label: Documented seller conversations; value: 150 conversations equal 30% of screened records; numeric value: 150.0; detail: Count only sellers who discuss debt terms and transaction objectives. The remaining 350 records never advance into documented underwriting during this cohort window.

label: Debt-and-title qualified opportunities; value: 45 opportunities equal 30% of seller conversations; numeric value: 45.0; detail: Require usable debt evidence, preliminary title findings, a priceable arrears position, and a credible acceleration response. These opportunities equal 9% of starting records.

label: Matched and underwritten wrap files; value: 12 files equal 26.7% of qualified opportunities; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Each file has a specific qualified buyer, licensed RMLO review, documented repayment analysis, and counsel-reviewed structure. These files equal 2.4% of starting records.

label: Funded and servicer-boarded wraps; value: Six closings equal 50% of underwritten files; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Count only executed closings with confirmed funding, recording submission, servicing setup, and an underlying payment schedule. Final conversion equals 1.2% of records.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative six-month cohort, not observed conversion data. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Counts do not derive the $475,000 annual Base-Case revenue: annual retained interest also depends on the seasoned performing portfolio.
